conventions.margins: All race margins and poll averages are Democrat minus Republican in percentage points (positive = D ahead). poll_miss = actual margin - final poll average (positive = Democrats beat the polls). Exceptions noted (UT 2022, AK 2022, ME/VT independents, CA 2018 D-vs-D).

counting_speed_notes.AZ: Maricopa takes ~10-13 days (13 in 2024). Early ballots received before Election Day reported first at 10 pm ET (lean mixed/R in recent cycles), then Election Day votes (lean R since 2020), then 'late earlies' dropped off on Election Day counted over the following week (leaned D in 2022, R in 2024). 2024 bipartisan law (effective 2026) lets counties offer on-site ID for Election Day drop-offs to skip signature curing; HB 2703 (end most Election Day drop-offs) vetoed Feb 2025.
counting_speed_notes.PA: No pre-canvassing of mail ballots before 7 am Election Day. Election Day votes (R-leaning) often reported first in many counties -> red mirage, then blue shift as mail ballots (D-leaning) are added. Philadelphia/Allegheny finished most mail counting on election night in 2024; Senate was called ~1-2 am in 2022.
counting_speed_notes.CA: Weeks. Mail ballots postmarked by Election Day accepted 7 days later; late-counted ballots historically lean D (in 2022 they moved several House seats toward Dems). House control in 2022 waited on CA (Nov 16).
counting_speed_notes.NV: Mail ballots postmarked by Election Day accepted until 5 pm on the 4th day after (shortened from 7 days by 2025 law; upheld by SCOTUS ruling reported June 2026). Clark County reports in batches over several days; late mail leaned D in 2022, more mixed in 2024. Signature cure deadline extends further.
counting_speed_notes.GA: Fast. Early in-person and absentee votes (D-leaning) reported first after 7 pm; counties must report early vote by 8 pm under 2024 rules. Election Day votes lean R -> blue mirage then red shift. Runoff if no majority (Senate 2022 went to Dec 6).
counting_speed_notes.NC: Fast. Early/absentee vote (D-leaning) reported at 7:30 pm, Election Day precincts follow; ~95%+ counted on election night. Mail ballots must arrive by Election Day since 2023 law.
counting_speed_notes.FL: Very fast. Mail and early votes tabulated before close and dumped at 7/8 pm ET; most counties finished by ~9 pm ET. Statewide calls shortly after 8 pm ET when the Panhandle closes.
counting_speed_notes.TX: Fast. Early vote dump (now majority of ballots) at 8 pm ET; Election Day precincts trickle in. Harris County has been slow (hours to a day).
counting_speed_notes.MI: Faster since 2022: Prop 2 (2022) and 2023 law allow large jurisdictions to pre-process absentee ballots up to 8 days before Election Day; nine days of early in-person voting. Detroit absentee results still land late night. 2024 statewide results essentially complete by Wednesday morning.
counting_speed_notes.WI: No pre-processing: absentee ballots cannot be opened before 7 am Election Day. Milwaukee central count reports absentee ballots (heavily D) in one dump typically midnight-3 am CT -> late blue shift. Monday-processing bill not enacted as of late 2025. Senate called Wednesday in 2022.
counting_speed_notes.ME: Ranked-choice voting for federal races. If no majority, ballots transported to Augusta and tabulated over roughly a week (ME-2 called Nov 15 in 2018; Golden race took a week in 2022 and 2024). Also slow Election Day reporting from small towns.
counting_speed_notes.AK: Ranked-choice (top-four); absentee ballots accepted up to 10 days (domestic) / 15 days (overseas) after; RCV tabulation runs ~15 days after Election Day (Nov 18-ish). A 2026 initiative to repeal top-four/RCV is on the ballot (would not affect 2026 count). Polls close midnight ET.
counting_speed_notes.OH: Fast. Early/absentee reported first at 7:30 pm (D-leaning), then Election Day (R-leaning) -> red shift. Mail ballots postmarked by the day before and arriving within 4 days counted later but rarely decisive.
counting_speed_notes.IA: Fast; most results by ~midnight ET. Mail ballots must arrive by close of polls (2021 law).
counting_speed_notes.NE: Fast; mail must arrive by close of polls. Watch NE-2.
counting_speed_notes.CO: All-mail; ballots received through Election Day. Large early dump at 9 pm ET covers most votes; counting finishes within days.
counting_speed_notes.WA: All-mail, postmarked by Election Day; counts continue for 1-2 weeks and late ballots lean D (Murray 2022 margin grew from election night). Close House races take days.
counting_speed_notes.OR: All-mail, postmarked by Election Day (accepted 7 days after); most counted within a few days.
counting_speed_notes.UT: Mail-dominant; postmarked by day before Election Day; counting takes 1-2 weeks.
counting_speed_notes.NY: Historically slow absentee counting; since 2022-23 law absentee ballots are canvassed as received, so most results known election night. Mail ballots postmarked by Election Day accepted 7 days.
counting_speed_notes.MN: Fast; most results by late evening.
counting_speed_notes.KS: Fast; mail ballots postmarked by Election Day accepted 3 days after (repeal of grace period under litigation/legislative change - verify).
counting_speed_notes.NH: Fast on election night; paper ballots hand-counted in small towns but complete by ~midnight.
counting_speed_notes.VA: Fast; early votes reported first (since 2022 same-day report), then Election Day; late mail (postmarked by E-day, accepted 3 days) rarely decisive.
counting_speed_notes.MT: Mail-dominant; results late evening ET; close races may take until next day.
counting_speed_notes.NM: Fast; most results by midnight ET.
counting_speed_notes.general: Pattern: states that pre-process mail/early votes and report them first (FL, GA, NC, OH, TX, CO) show a 'blue mirage' then red shift; states that cannot pre-process (PA, WI) or count mail late (AZ, NV, CA, WA) show a 'red mirage' then blue shift. House control in 2022 took 8 days (Nov 16); Senate took 4 (Nov 12). In 2018 both chambers were called on election night.
